segments.say: Lesson 20. Lang Smith & L L M Observability. Traces, runs, datasets, experiments, prompt hub, online evaluators and monitoring dashboards.

Lang Smith is a platform that records every step of your L L M app (a trace) and lets you build datasets, run experiments and monitor quality in production. It's observability for A I apps. Here is an analogy. A flight recorder plus a test lab: every request's journey is recorded, so when something goes wrong you replay it and see exactly which step failed.

Why does this matter? Debugging L L M apps without traces is guesswork. Observability and evaluation tooling comes up in every production-A I interview. A few key words. Trace: The full record of one request. Run / span: One step inside a trace (retriever, L L M call, tool). Dataset: Saved examples for testing. Experiment: An app version run against a dataset with evaluators.
Anatomy of a trace. A trace records one end-to-end request, made of nested runs (spans) for every step. Turn it on with an A P I key plus LANGSMITH TRACING=true, or @traceable on any function.
Each run captures inputs, outputs, latency, token usage, cost and errors. You can see exactly which chunks were retrieved and the exact prompt the model saw.
Debugging superpower: open a bad answer, see the retrieved context was wrong, and you know it's a retrieval bug, in seconds.
Save interesting traces to a dataset, then run experiments (app version times dataset times evaluators) and compare versions side by side.
In production: dashboards (latency, cost, error rate), user feedback attached to traces, and online evaluators scoring sampled traffic, with alerts on drops.

What Lang Smith gives you. Tracing for Lang Chain/Lang Graph automatically, and any code via @traceable or the OpenTelemetry integration. Datasets & experiments: offline evals with custom and L L M-judge evaluators, comparison views. Prompt Hub / playground: version prompts, test them against datasets. Annotation queues: humans label traces. Online evaluators, rules & alerts: monitor production quality. Framework-agnostic: works without Lang Chain too.

Alternatives you should name. Langfuse (open source, self-hostable), Arize Phoenix (OpenTelemetry-native), Weights & Biases Weave, Helicone (proxy-based), Datadog / Splunk L L M observability. Emerging standard: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions for L L M spans.

What to monitor in production. Latency: time-to-first-token and total, p50/p95/p99. Tokens & cost per request, per user, per feature. Error rates: provider 429s/5xx, tool failures, parse failures. Quality: online judge scores, thumbs-down rate, escalation rate. Drift: query topics changing, retrieval-hit rate dropping.

Say it in the interview. "Every request is traced end to end in Lang Smith (retrieval, rerank, model call, tool calls) with tokens, cost and latency per span. Failing traces become dataset examples, prompt changes run as experiments against them, and production has online evaluators plus dashboards and alerts on latency, cost and quality. With Splunk in the stack I'd also export OpenTelemetry spans for unified observability.".

Let's compare. Lang Smith: managed (self-host on enterprise), deep Lang Chain/Lang Graph integration, evals, prompt hub. Langfuse: open source, self-host, tracing plus evals plus prompt mgmt. Arize Phoenix: open source, OpenTelemetry-native, eval library. Helicone: proxy / gateway, drop-in logging, caching, cost. Splunk / Datadog: A P M platforms, L L M spans next to infra metrics.

A likely interview question: What do you monitor for an L L M app in prod? A strong answer: Latency (T T F T, p95), tokens and cost per request and feature, errors (rate limits, tool and parse failures), quality signals (online judge scores, feedback, escalations) and drift. All traced per request with alerts.
That's it for Lang Smith & L L M Observability. Now play the quiz and games in the app to lock it in. See you in the next lesson.
